- **Substantive design decisions documented:**
  - **`jcs_serialize` from in-tree `services.audit.chain`, NOT `jcs.canonicalize` from PyJCS.** Dev-guide §5.2 illustrates the SSE emitter with `import jcs; jcs.canonicalize(envelope)`. PyJCS raises `TypeError` on `Decimal` values, which the trading system uses pervasively for money/price (anti-pattern A05). The audit-chain module's `jcs_serialize` is A05-aware — it accepts Decimal-as-string and rejects bare `float`. Today's SSE envelope shape doesn't yet include Decimal values (the per-event-type data shapes for signal/fill/position from spec §4.2.2 are NOT in Day 16 scope; only the envelope wrapper + `ping` data shape lands today), but using the in-tree canonicalizer NOW means the dispatcher Week 4 Wed PR can pass Decimal-bearing data dicts to `emit_sse()` without per-call re-coercion. Pre-empts a Day-N+M lesson where someone emits a fill with `Decimal("5234.50")` and PyJCS throws.
  - **`ping` event type accepted at canonical-taxonomy gate, lands in replay buffer.** IG §3 Week 5 Tue gate language is literal: "`event: ping` lines every 30s". The Day-5 `: keepalive` comment-line emission did NOT satisfy the gate text (comments are filtered out by the EventSource client). Day 16 emits a real SSE event with `type=ping`, `data={"server_now": "..."}`, `sequence_no` incrementing per heartbeat. Pings DO get a sequence_no AND DO land in the replay buffer per spec §4.2.1 ("GLOBAL monotonic across all event types"); a reconnecting client with Last-Event-ID gets every missed ping replayed in order. The alternative (skip pings from replay) would violate the "global monotonic" lock — replay would have gaps where pings used to be.
  - **Replay buffer pruned by timestamp + hard-cap safety valve.** Spec §4.2.3 says "24h backend retention". The canonical implementation is timestamp-based: on every emit, pop entries from the LEFT of the deque while `entry.server_now < now - 24h`. ALSO enforce a hard ceiling of 1M entries as a safety valve against an emit-storm bug filling RAM (1M @ ~500 bytes/entry ≈ 500MB, well below the api container's 1GB RAM allocation in `deploy/docker-compose.yml`). Under normal Phase-0 emit volume the timestamp prune drops entries well before the count matters; the hard cap exists for robustness, not as a normal load-shedding mechanism. The dev-guide §5.2 example uses a count-based heuristic ("keep last 100k events") with a TODO for the timestamp impl; Day 16 replaces that with the real timestamp impl.
  - **`session_evicted` reason vocabulary locked at `tab_limit` today; other 3 reasons documented but not wired.** Spec §4.2.2 + frontend-spec §4.6 lock 4 reasons: `tab_limit`, `explicit_logout`, `breakglass_kill`, `creds_rotated`. Only `tab_limit` has a producer in Day 16 scope (the multiplexer's `register_subscriber` enforces N=4 last-connected-wins). The other 3 wire at their respective lifecycle points: `explicit_logout` when the auth ceremony lands Week 6; `breakglass_kill` when the breakglass operator action lands Phase 1+; `creds_rotated` when the secret-rotation flow lands Phase 1+. The `SessionEvictionReason: Literal` already includes all 4 so the future PRs only need to extend the producer logic; the multiplexer accepts any of the 4 in `_evict_subscriber()`.
  - **Backpressure drops do NOT receive a `session_evicted` envelope.** Per-subscriber queue is `asyncio.Queue(maxsize=500)`. If a subscriber's queue is full when `emit_sse()` tries to enqueue, the multiplexer logs a `sse_subscriber_dropped_full_queue` warning and calls `_evict_subscriber(sub, "tab_limit")` — but does NOT push a `session_evicted` envelope first. Rationale: the queue is full, the frame wouldn't fit anyway; the client receives an EOF, reconnects per spec §4.2.3 + frontend-spec §4.5 with a Last-Event-ID, and the replay buffer catches them up. This is canonical SSE backpressure and matches dev-guide §5.2's `dead` list pattern. The `tab_limit` reason is reused for backpressure drops because the client's recovery path is identical (reconnect + Last-Event-ID); future PRs could split into a dedicated `backpressure_drop` reason if frontend telemetry needs to distinguish, but that's a frontend-spec change.
  - **N=4 eviction emits the `session_evicted` envelope BEFORE setting `evict_event`.** Ordering matters here. If `evict_event` is set first, the evicted subscriber's stream generator may exit its `asyncio.wait` loop before the eviction envelope reaches its queue, and the client gets an EOF with no reason. Today's `register_subscriber` calls `_emit_session_evicted_to(oldest, "tab_limit")` (sync; uses `put_nowait`) FIRST so the envelope is in the queue; THEN `_evict_subscriber(oldest, "tab_limit")` marks the evict_event. The generator wakes from `queue.get()` with the envelope, yields it to the client, then on the next iteration sees `evict_event.is_set()` and exits. Locked-in by the `TestTabLimitEviction::test_evicted_subscriber_receives_session_evicted_envelope` test which fishes the envelope out of `oldest.queue`.
  - **Route layer is intentionally thin; the heavy lifting lives in `services/api/sse.py`.** The route handler in `services/api/routes/sse.py` is ~90 lines: parse `Last-Event-ID`, dispatch to either the 426 path or the live-stream path, register a subscriber, wrap the per-subscriber generator in a `StreamingResponse`, deregister in `finally`. All the multiplexer state + envelope + JCS + replay + eviction + heartbeat logic lives in `services/api/sse.py`. Same shape as the `services/risk/state_machine.py` (pure-policy plan) → `services/risk/dispatcher.py` (eventually) split that Week 4 Wed will introduce — the policy module is testable without a FastAPI app at all (40 of the 50 Day 16 tests don't go through the route; only `TestRoute` and `TestSessionExemptPathsUpdated` touch the FastAPI layer).
  - **Lenient `Last-Event-ID` parsing.** A malformed/negative/zero `Last-Event-ID` header is treated as a fresh-connect (not 4xx). Rationale: the EventSource spec doesn't constrain the header format, our server-emitted ids are always decimal integers, and a non-int means a buggy/cached header — better to reconnect cleanly than to return 4xx and force the client to flush the cache before it can reconnect. Locked-in by the 5 `_parse_last_event_id` unit tests.
  - **Phase-2 deferral documented in module docstring.** The single-process, in-memory design is explicit for Phase 0. Phase 2 (multi-replica) migrates: sequence counter → Redis INCR or Postgres advisory-lock + sequence; replay buffer → Redis stream with ~24h MAXLEN OR Postgres table with TTL pruning; subscriber tracking → unchanged. The public `emit_sse` + route surface does NOT change; tests written today against in-memory state exercise the same public contract Phase 2 will support.
  - **`tests/unit/test_api_sse.py` avoids `httpx.AsyncClient.stream("GET", "/api/sse/events")` for the live-stream test.** ASGITransport doesn't release in-memory streams until the body is fully consumed, but the multiplexer's live stream never closes (intentional — it's a long-lived SSE channel). A naive `async with api_client.stream(...) as response: assert response.status_code == 200` hangs forever waiting for body completion. The Day 16 test workaround calls the route handler `sse_events(request=stub_request, session=stub_session)` directly, asserts `isinstance(response, StreamingResponse)` + headers + that `multiplexer._test_subscriber_count("u-route") == 1`, then aborts via `response.body_iterator.aclose()`. The 426 path's test DOES use `api_client.get(...)` because that path returns a one-shot stream (single must-reload frame, then exits) — `_single_frame_stream` yields one frame then returns, which lets ASGITransport release.

- **Substantive design decisions documented in code:**
  - **DP-020: server-level `write 24h` (option a) over per-route override (b) or h1 downgrade (c).** Per the DP-020 register row above: option (a) is the smallest diff (single integer change in an existing block), matches the existing `idle 24h` philosophy, doesn't require new Caddyfile concepts, and is fully reversible. Option (b) (per-route header overrides) isn't expressible in Caddyfile syntax for h2 stream-level timeouts. Option (c) (h1 downgrade) would require a global directive and lose multiplexing benefits for non-SSE routes that share the listener. The non-SSE write-timeout risk surface from option (a) is bounded because (i) non-SSE responses complete in milliseconds, (ii) the new api-side `RateLimitMiddleware` (100 req/10s per IP) caps abuse, (iii) Caddy's connection-level idle timeout still applies.
  - **Rate limiting at api layer rather than Caddy.** `caddy:2-alpine` (the image in `docker-compose.yml`) doesn't include the `mholt/caddy-ratelimit` community plugin. Two paths considered: (1) xcaddy custom build → bigger PR (new Caddy Dockerfile + image push to GHCR + docker-compose change to use the new image tag), more moving parts; (2) Pydantic-Settings-configured `RateLimitMiddleware` at the FastAPI layer → stays on `services/api/**` hot-fix whitelist, fully unit-tested via existing TestClient pattern, no image rebuild, knobs tunable via `deploy/.env` (`API_RATE_LIMIT_GENERAL_PER_WINDOW=200` etc.) without redeploy. Chose (2). Operator-facing tradeoff documented: rate limits trigger *after* hitting api container, not at Caddy edge — so a flood would still reach uvicorn before getting 429'd. For Phase 0 with single-replica api behind Caddy on the internal Docker network (no public port exposed), this is acceptable; Phase 1 may revisit if real load justifies Caddy-edge filtering.
  - **Fixed-window counter, not sliding-window or token-bucket.** The IG spec contract is "N per window" which fixed-window satisfies exactly. Known burst-at-window-edge property (up to 2N requests in a 2-second span straddling a window boundary) is acceptable for Phase 0; sliding-window is a Phase 1 hardening candidate if real attack data shows the edge-burst being exploited.
  - **`_monotonic()` module-level indirection over `time.monotonic` direct call.** The middleware imports `_monotonic` from its own module so tests can monkeypatch it — the test fixture `deterministic_clock` replaces `_monotonic` with a closure over a 1-element list, and tests advance time by mutating `store[0]`. No `asyncio.sleep` or `freezegun` dependency required. Pattern lifted from existing dev-guide §6.x test-injection idioms.
  - **`register_middleware` reordering with explicit "last-added = outermost" empirical verification.** The pre-Day-17 `register_middleware` had a comment claiming `last-added = outermost`, while a separate comment in `services/api/main.py` claimed `last-added = innermost` — these contradicted. Day 17 work resolved this by writing a 20-line one-shot Starlette test that registered three sentinel middleware classes A/B/C and printed enter/exit traces (`C enter / B enter / A enter / ROUTE / A exit / B exit / C exit` — proving C, the last-added, is OUTERMOST). The new `register_middleware` ordering reflects this: CSRF added first (now innermost of the four), RateLimit second (outer of CSRF — so floods consume bucket slots even when CSRF would have rejected them), RequestContext third (outermost of the three in `register_middleware`; binds trace_id for all logs from inner middlewares). The Day-5 `main.py` claim that SessionStub is "innermost" was empirically wrong (SessionStub is added LAST so it's OUTERMOST of all four), but the existing code works regardless because SessionStub only mutates `request.state.session` and never short-circuits, so the order didn't affect functional behavior. Today's PR does NOT fix the stale `main.py` comment — that's a Day 18+ doc-hygiene follow-up; the SessionStub ordering will be revisited when the real WebAuthn middleware lands Week 6.
  - **404 paths as rate-limit-test probes.** `/api/__rl_test` and `/api/auth/__rl_test` don't have FastAPI route handlers — they return 404 from the router. But middleware runs BEFORE routing, so the counter increments. This decouples rate-limit tests from route-handler DB dependencies (every Day-15 Phase-1 REST route uses `dependency_overrides` for the repo, which would be redundant boilerplate here). The exempt-path tests use real handlers (`/api/health` with `api_db.ping` monkeypatched) to exercise the exemption decision through to a real 200.

Day 17 first attempt did this and pytest hung indefinitely. Resolution: factor the exemption-decision logic into `RateLimitMiddleware._select_bucket(path)` and test it via direct method call from `test_sse_endpoint_exemption_decision`. Documented in the test docstring. The N=4 tab cap inside the SSE multiplexer already bounds per-user concurrency, so missing rate-limit coverage on SSE is acceptable.

- **Substantive design decisions documented:**
  - **Caddy reload alone is insufficient post-`git pull`; force-recreate is the canonical pattern.** Docker bind mounts of single files capture the inode at mount time. `git pull`'s atomic-rename update flow creates a new inode for the file, leaving the container's bind mount pointing at the OLD inode. `caddy reload` reads `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile` inside the container — which is still the old inode — so the "reload" succeeds but applies stale content. The fix is `docker compose up -d --force-recreate caddy`, which re-resolves the bind mount path and exposes the host's current file content. This was the FIRST surprise of the carryover and consumed ~3 minutes of debug time; the runbook's Step 2 is updated to prevent recurrence. **Alternative considered + rejected:** mount the entire `deploy/` directory instead of the single `Caddyfile` (directory bind mounts re-resolve on each `open()` and aren't inode-pinned). Rejected because (a) it'd pull in `deploy/api/README.md` and other unrelated files into Caddy's container scope, and (b) `force-recreate` is a one-line runbook addition that's already idiomatic for the rest of the deploy.
  - **UFW DENY does NOT block Docker-published ports — `docker compose stop caddy` is the real outage simulation.** Docker's iptables rules for `-p 443:443` published ports sit in the `DOCKER` chain which runs BEFORE UFW's `INPUT` chain (via the `FORWARD` jump). UFW INPUT rules only filter traffic destined to the host's own services (not Docker containers). The IG text's `ufw deny 443` recipe is incorrect for this Docker setup — it leaves UFW status showing DENY but external traffic still reaches the container. The actually-correct mechanism is `docker compose stop caddy` (or `docker compose pause caddy`, but `stop` cleanly closes the listening socket → external curl gets connection refused, which is what we want to simulate). **Alternative considered + rejected:** add `iptables -I DOCKER-USER -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP` to drop traffic in the `DOCKER-USER` chain (which runs before `DOCKER` chain and is Docker's official escape hatch for custom rules). Rejected because (a) the rule needs to be removed for the auto-revert and the cleanup is more error-prone than `at`-scheduled `docker compose start caddy`, (b) `docker compose stop caddy` more accurately models the failure mode the watchdog is designed to detect (the Caddy container crashed/exited), (c) operator-level reasoning ("the proxy is down") is clearer than iptables-level reasoning ("packets are getting dropped at the DOCKER-USER chain"). **Day 17 carryover updates `deploy/api/README.md` Step 5 (Week 5 gate box 3) to document this** so the next operator running this gate doesn't repeat the UFW mistake.
  - **`at`-scheduled auto-restart is the canonical "outage test" safety mechanism.** Even though my Claude Code session is currently alive, scheduling the recovery action with `at` decouples the restoration from session liveness. If my Mac sleeps mid-test, the SSH connection dies, the operator closes the laptop, etc., the VPS still self-heals at the scheduled time. The runbook's "Step 6 Rollback path" already documented this idea for the rate-limit middleware (operator can rollback via `deploy/.env` overrides without redeploy); extending it to the outage-test mechanism is the same principle. `atq` post-schedule confirms job is queued. The at-job's stdout/stderr lands in `/var/log/ufw_test.log` and the operator can `grep CADDY_RESTART_DONE /var/log/ufw_test.log` after the scheduled time to confirm it fired.
  - **Two-surface SSE smoke pattern is now CANONICAL for any SSE-related deploy.** Day 16 carryover originated it (loopback + external curl); Day 17 carryover re-validated it (loopback unchanged + external NOW PASSES post-DP-020-fix). Future SSE feature work (Week 6+ event-type expansion, Phase 1 dispatcher real-event emission, Phase 2 multi-replica state migration) should adopt the same two-surface ritual.
  - **Rate-limit verification needs parallel curls for the general bucket.** The IG Week 5 Fri operator test prescribes `for i in $(seq 1 110); do curl ... ; done` — sequential. With sequential curls at ~50-100ms TLS+round-trip each, 110 requests easily span >10s, which crosses the rate-limit window boundary. The first run of the verification got 110 × 200 (false negative — counter reset mid-loop). The fix is `xargs -P 30 -n1 -I{}` to parallelize. The runbook's Step 5 should be updated to use parallel curls. **Did NOT update the IG Week 5 Fri text** (that's the operator's eventual test prose; the runbook addition + this decisions-log entry are the discoverable doc trail). Optional follow-up: update IG Week 5 Fri text to match the parallel-curls pattern.

- **Substantive design decisions documented in code:**
  - **Plan-then-apply pattern faithful to PR #42 (recon) precedent.** The planner is pure: same inputs → same `CalibrationPlan`; no I/O; no audit writes; no DB reads. The dispatcher (Week 4) owns: (1) the audit write via `services.audit.writer.append_audit_event(plan.audit_event.event_type, plan.audit_event.payload)` capturing the `audit_event_uuid`; (2) the row INSERT into `slippage_calibration_versions` with the captured UUID + the planner-supplied `new_version_id` + `version_no` + JSONB-serialized `per_market_coefficients` + `data_window_*` + `calibrated_at_utc` + trigger.value; (3) conditionally on `becomes_head`, the HEAD-pointer swap inside ONE transaction (`UPDATE ... SET is_head = FALSE WHERE is_head` then `UPDATE ... SET is_head = TRUE WHERE id = :new_version_id`; the partial unique index `slippage_head` makes a partial swap raise rather than leave dual-HEAD state). This isolation — planner returns a struct as data; caller is the I/O boundary — is the standard for everything in `services/risk/`, `services/scheduler/`, `services/qc_adapter/`, `services/reconciliation/`. Future dispatcher PR (Week 4 work; separate forbidden-whitelist PR) wires `plan_calibration_fit` into the monthly cron + bootstrap call site.
  - **Per-market OLS, NOT portfolio-level.** Per backend-spec §2.14 functional form `slippage_bps_market = alpha_market + beta_market * (order_size / ADV_30d)` — the spec text explicitly tags both intercept + slope with `_market` subscripts. Hence `CalibrationPlan.per_market_coefficients: Mapping[str, MarketCoefficient]` rather than a single (alpha, beta, r_squared) on the plan. This also matches the §3.12 schema column `per_market_coefficients JSONB` shape `{"MES": {...}, "ES": {...}, ...}` exactly — the audit payload + the JSONB row will be byte-identical for chain-verifier reconstruction. The `plan_calibration_fit` briefing-shape sketch was orientation-only ("don't copy verbatim; read §2.14 first") and the briefing's single-alpha-beta hint was a simplification; the real spec contract requires per-market.
  - **MIN_OBSERVATIONS_FOR_OLS = 30 applied per market, not portfolio-wide.** Per spec §2.14 "first real calibration after 30 days of Phase 1 LIVE fills" — interpreted as "30 fills per market" rather than "30 fills total" because the regression is per-market. This means the dispatcher's monthly cron will fan out across markets and a market that hasn't hit 30 fills yet keeps its zero-prior coefficients (alpha=0, beta=0) rather than fitting on a small noisy sample. The two-tiered fallback (per-market + plan-level) is documented in the calibration.py docstring's "Two fit methods" block.
  - **Plan-level fit_method label = `OLS` when ANY market crosses MIN_OBSERVATIONS_FOR_OLS threshold, else `ZERO_PRIOR`.** The first-iteration logic checked `r_squared is not None` to detect OLS, but that fails on the constant-x degenerate branch (Sxx=0 → r_squared=None even though n_obs >= 30). The fix is to use `n_obs >= MIN_OBSERVATIONS_FOR_OLS` as the threshold-crossing signal. This caught one failing test (`TestNonBootstrapFallback::test_mixed_market_one_ols_one_fallback_labels_plan_ols`) which exercises a real-world edge case (one market has 30 identical-size fills, another has 5 fills — MES should be OLS-labeled even though the regressor is constant; ES is zero-prior; plan label is OLS because at least one market ran through the estimator). Discussed in calibration.py's `plan_calibration_fit` body comment.
  - **Slippage sign convention: `+bps = cost to trader`.** For a buy, `+slippage_bps` means the realized price was higher than expected (trader paid more); for a sell, `+slippage_bps` means the realized price was lower than expected (trader received less). Both fold into a single signed Decimal via the direction multiplier. This is the standard finance convention and matches what spec §2.14's functional form implies (a positive beta on size/ADV means larger orders cost more to execute — only makes sense if `+slippage_bps` is "cost to trader"). Unit-test fixtures in TestSlippageSignConvention lock all 4 sign permutations.
  - **Decimal-only OLS arithmetic, no float promotion.** Following dev-guide §3.8 + A05: every step of the regression — `xbar`, `ybar`, `Sxx`, `Sxy`, `Syy`, `beta`, `alpha`, `r_squared` — uses Decimal operations (sum + product + division). Decimal default precision is 28 digits which is more than enough for the bps-scale numbers we're fitting on; tests TestOLSFit confirm the hand-computed `y = 2 + 4x` returns `beta=4, alpha=2, r_squared=1` to 4 decimal places. Float promotion would risk subtle accumulator drift across the 30+ fills × 5+ markets the dispatcher will call this with monthly. The cost is `Decimal` is slower than `float` by ~10× for arithmetic — irrelevant for a once-per-month cron over ≤1000 fills.
  - **Caller-supplied `new_version_id` (UUID) rather than planner-generated.** The planner does NOT call `uuid_v7()` directly. The caller passes in a UUIDv7 that flows into both the `CalibrationPlan.new_version_id` AND the audit event payload's `new_version_id` field. This keeps the planner pure (same inputs → same plan) and matches the recon precedent where `account_id` + `contract_id` are caller-side. The dispatcher will generate the UUID once before invoking the planner, use it for the audit write + the row INSERT — both rows reference the same UUID end-to-end.
  - **Caller-supplied `parent_version_no` for monotonic increment, no DB read in the planner.** The planner returns `version_no = parent_version_no + 1` (or 1 if None). The caller-side dispatcher reads `SELECT max(version_no) FROM slippage_calibration_versions` BEFORE invoking the planner and passes the result in. This is symmetric with the existing `services/qc_adapter/poll.py` cursor pattern and keeps the planner DB-free. A small race exists between read-max + insert-new — the table's `version_no UNIQUE` constraint catches it (the INSERT raises a uniqueness violation if a concurrent calibration grabbed the same number) and the dispatcher retries with the new max. For Phase 1 this is a non-issue — calibration is a monthly cron, single-writer.
  - **`becomes_head` default True with explicit False reserved for "compute-but-don't-promote" research.** The Phase 1 monthly cron + bootstrap should default to swapping the HEAD pointer to the new version (the operational norm). A future Phase 1+ research path may want to compute calibration coefficients without promoting them (e.g., shadow-fit comparisons, A/B testing). Setting `becomes_head=False` writes the audit + row but leaves `is_head=FALSE` on the new row. The partial unique index doesn't fire because no row has `is_head=TRUE` set in the swap — the existing HEAD stays HEAD. The audit payload includes `becomes_head` so the chain verifier can distinguish "this calibration was promoted" from "this was a research compute".
  - **Iterable input + internal tuple consumption.** `plan_calibration_fit(fills=...)` accepts `Iterable[FillObservation]` (not just tuple/list) so callers can pass generators. The planner immediately consumes into a tuple (`fill_tuple = tuple(fills)`) so it can be iterated multiple times for window math + per-market grouping + OLS fit without re-iteration concerns. TestIterableInput locks this contract (a generator input produces the expected fill_count + data_window).
  - **Greek-letter convention: ASCII-only in comments + docstrings.** Initial draft used Greek symbols (`α`, `β`, `Σ`, `×`, `²`, `x̄`, `ȳ`) for math notation in docstrings + comments. Ruff RUF002 + RUF003 + RUF004 flag these as "ambiguous Unicode" because they look like ASCII letters in some fonts (`α` could be confused with `a`). The project's pyproject.toml ruff config doesn't ignore these rules, and no other in-tree file uses Greek letters in comments. Replaced with plain-English equivalents (`alpha`, `beta`, `xbar`, `ybar`, `Sxx`, `Sxy`, `Syy`, `**2`, `*`) — the math reads identically and stays grep-able. The pattern of "ASCII-only in comments + docstrings" is now the de facto repo convention; future PRs adding math-heavy comments should follow.

- **Three small live-discovered fixes during pnpm/docker smoke:**
  - **Next 14.2.20 → 14.2.35 (Dec 2025 security advisory).** First `pnpm install` succeeded but emitted `WARN deprecated next@14.2.20: This version has a security vulnerability. Please upgrade to a patched version.` Per `npm view next@14 dist-tags`, the `next-14` tag points to 14.2.35 (latest patched in the 14.2 line). Bumped both `next` and `eslint-config-next` to 14.2.35 with exact pins (no `^`/`~` per the brief lock). `pnpm install` post-bump removed the deprecation warning. The remaining `WARN deprecated eslint@8.57.1` is informational only — `eslint-config-next` 14.2.x is pinned to ESLint 8 by design, and bumping ESLint would require bumping `eslint-config-next` which requires bumping Next, which is out of scope.
  - **`addgroup: gid '1000' in use` on `node:20-alpine` runtime stage.** First Dockerfile mirrored the api Dockerfile pattern (`groupadd --gid 1000 trading + useradd --uid 1000 --gid trading`) which works against `python:3.11-slim` because that base image doesn't have a 1000 user. `node:20-alpine` already ships the `node` user at uid/gid 1000 (the canonical Node Docker non-root convention). Two options: (a) reuse the existing `node` user, (b) bump trading to uid/gid 1001. Chose (a) — matches the canonical Node Docker pattern + still satisfies the dev-guide §3 / backend-spec §8.11 non-root requirement + avoids cosmetic uid 1001 drift from the api/webhook_pusher pattern (the COPY `--chown=node:node` lines make the intent obvious in the Dockerfile).
  - **Docker build context = `apps/web/`, not repo root.** First build sent 315MB of build context up front (entire repo trees including `node_modules/`, `.next/`, `services/`, `tests/`, `Docs/`, `secrets/`, the existing api + webhook_pusher containers' image layers, etc.). The api + webhook_pusher Dockerfiles use `context: .` because they need repo-root-relative paths (`pyproject.toml`, `services/`, `infrastructure/`, `strategies/`, `alembic/`). The nextjs container only consumes `apps/web/` source — there's no benefit to repo-root context, just cost. Switched `docker-compose.yml` `nextjs.build.context` from `.` to `apps/web` and the Dockerfile's COPY paths from `apps/web/package.json` to `package.json` etc. Build context dropped to apps/web subtree (still includes node_modules + .next from the local dev install, but apps/web/.dockerignore filters those out — apps/web's .dockerignore now applies correctly because it sits at the context root). When Phase 1+ adds `packages/api-types` as a shared TypeScript dependency, the context bumps back to repo root + a top-level `.dockerignore` will need to exclude services/* tests/* etc. — flagged as a Day 21+ follow-up only if/when that dependency lands.

The DB stores `nonce(12 bytes) || ciphertext+tag` as BYTEA; tampered ciphertext surfaces as `cryptography.exceptions.InvalidTag` and is wrapped to 503 by the route handler. Backend-spec §8.5.2 "separate from sops" is interpreted as "separate KEY from the sops master age key, but still distributed via sops at rest" — the standard column-encryption pattern.

Argon2id-hashed at rest (same hasher as `setup_tokens`: time_cost=3, memory_cost=64 MiB, parallelism=4, hash_len=32, salt_len=16). Raw codes returned exactly once via `POST /api/auth/backup-codes/generate` response; subsequent retrieval is impossible.

- **Substantive design decisions captured in code:**
  - **Single `useSSE()` mount at page level (`page.tsx`) rather than per-component.** Spec §4.1 LOCKED is "single multiplexed channel: `GET /api/sse/events`" — the backend's N=4 tab cap also applies per-user across all browser tabs. Mounting `useSSE` from multiple components would open multiple SSE connections from a single tab and rapidly hit the N=4 cap as the operator opens additional tabs. Future pages (Trades, Performance, System) should NOT re-mount `useSSE` — the hook's invalidations on every event are global to the QueryClient, so the Today-page mount serves all visible pages.
  - **Cache-invalidation map (sse.ts `INVALIDATE_KEYS`) mirrors spec §8.6 verbatim.** Every event type lists the TanStack Query keys it invalidates. `ping` + `session_evicted` + `job` + `version` are control events with empty arrays (no business-data invalidation). Phase 0 SSE produces only `ping` events (no real `signal`/`fill`/`position` emitter until Week 4 Wed dispatcher); but the wiring is in place so the invalidation cascade works end-to-end when data lands.
  - **`session_evicted` envelope terminates the SSE connection.** Server-side the multiplexer closes the connection after sending `session_evicted`; client-side `sse.ts` catches the envelope, fires a P1 toast (or P0 for `breakglass_kill`/`creds_rotated`), and transitions to terminal `evicted` state — no auto-reconnect since the server explicitly evicted this tab. Operator must refresh manually to reconnect.
  - **Approve/Reject/Defer buttons call the 501-stub Day 15 endpoints, not nothing.** The mutations fire real network requests; the `SIGNAL_HANDLER_NOT_WIRED` ApiError surfaces a P2 toast explaining the handler isn't wired yet. This proves the end-to-end button-click → mutation → API → toast loop today, so when the Week 4 Wed dispatcher PR lands the handlers, the buttons work with zero frontend changes. Alternative (greying out the buttons until Phase 1) was rejected — operator should see the canonical error envelope today as the contract.
  - **Phase-0 `DecisionDiaryEntry` placeholder for reject/defer.** The Day 15 schema requires a `decision_diary_entry` body on reject/defer with min 10 char `reasoning_text`. Spec §3.1 ships the full DecisionDiaryModal in Phase 1. Day 22 sends a constant placeholder (`manual_judgment` tag + the literal "Phase-0 placeholder — DecisionDiaryModal lands Phase 1 (frontend-spec §3.1).") so the button click reaches the 501 stub end-to-end. The Phase-1 modal replaces the constant with a real form.
  - **Exposure cluster limits are hard-coded placeholders.** Spec §2.2.2 D shows the bars rendering against ring/cluster limits from the risk envelope. The `/api/system/risk-envelope` endpoint is a Phase 1+ wiring (not in Day 15 scope). Day 22 hard-codes the limits from the §2.2.1 layout example (`equity_idx: 60%, rates_bonds: 80%, commodity: 80%, crypto: 40%, fx: 60%`, `gross: 300%`, `net: 150%`). When the endpoint lands the component swaps to reading from a new `useRiskEnvelope()` hook; Day 22 ships the visual + interaction layer.
  - **No Zustand stores Day 22.** Spec §8.4 recommends Zustand for "UI-only state that doesn't belong in query cache" — cmdk-open, drawer stack, toast IDs, filter state. Day 22 has none of these: cmdk-open is a Phase-1 CommandPalette component; drawer is Phase-2; toasts are managed by the new `toast.ts` module-level store (lighter than Zustand for the single-mount Toaster case); filters are per-page Phase-1. Wiring an empty Zustand provider today adds a dep without exercising the contract. Day 23+ revisits when a real UI-only state need emerges.
  - **No `decimal.js` install.** Spec §8.10 reserves `decimal.js` for unavoidable frontend arithmetic. Per §8.9 LOCKED, the backend computes everything; Day 22 only displays pre-computed strings. Phase 0 returns Decimal-as-string `"0"` payloads which `format.ts` renders via native `Number(x).toFixed(2)`. The `decimal.js` install lands Day 22+ when a component actually needs to subtract/sum strings on the client (e.g., a future "select N rows to compute total P&L" feature).
  - **`@microsoft/fetch-event-source` chosen over native `EventSource`** per spec §4.1 — native cannot send custom headers (`Last-Event-ID` is the only allowed one), cannot expose connection lifecycle for backoff control, uses opaque auto-retry. Day 20 already installed the dep; Day 22 wires it.
  - **`useToasts` via `useSyncExternalStore` not Zustand.** The toast queue is a textbook external-store case: single global subscriber (the `<Toaster>` mount), imperative `toast(...)` callers from any component, no per-component reactive selectors needed. `useSyncExternalStore` is React's canonical primitive for this pattern; pulling Zustand in just for this would be overkill.
  - **`'use client'` directive on every component except `layout.tsx`.** The 8 Today-page components all use hooks (TanStack Query + the toast/SSE store) so they MUST be client-side. `layout.tsx` stays server-side (it has no hooks); the client boundary lives at `<Providers>`. This matches the Next.js 14 App Router idiom + dev-guide §4.3.
  - **Module-level singleton QueryClient (not `useState(() => new QueryClient())`).** Per `apps/web/src/lib/queryClient.ts` module export. TanStack docs recommend a stable client across renders; the alternative `useState` pattern survives StrictMode double-render but is friendly to per-test instance injection (future Vitest fixture). Day 22 chose the simpler singleton; the Day 23+ test framework can introduce a `Providers` prop for test-injection without breaking call sites.
  - **No optimistic updates Day 22.** Spec §8.5 LOCKED optimistic UX needs a real server handler for the round-trip — otherwise every approve flickers between "optimistically approved" and "501 rolled back". When the dispatcher lands (Week 4 Wed in implementation calendar; ahead of frontend's Week 7 Mon real-data swap), the optimistic-update pattern layers on without breaking the existing `useApproveSignal` / `useRejectSignal` / `useDeferSignal` call sites.

- **Decision: path naming `services/discord_bot/` (underscore) over `services/discord-bot/` (hyphen).** Spec dev-guide §2.1 + §2.3 listed `discord-bot/` (hyphen) but Python's import system cannot import dotted names containing hyphens. The two paths to make hyphen work — (a) separate `pyproject.toml` inside `services/discord-bot/` with `src/discord_bot/` layout, or (b) `sys.path` manipulation — both add non-trivial CI complexity (separate pip install + module-path manipulation) for zero functional benefit over the underscore directory. The existing scaffold at `services/discord_bot/__init__.py` was already underscore. The IG line 383 reference was already underscore. The `webhook_pusher/` + `qc_adapter/` precedents use underscore. Day 23 lands `services/discord_bot/` AND fixes dev-guide §2.1 + §2.3 inline to match — same surgical 3-char change as Day 20 PR #66's `frontend/` → `apps/web/` precedent (small doc fix bundled with the implementing PR).
- **Decision: api-side `BotAuthMiddleware` runs OUTERMOST.** The middleware order after Day 23 becomes `BotAuth → SessionStub → RequestContext → RateLimit → CSRF → routes`. BotAuth must run before SessionStub because in live envs SessionStub fail-closes (HTTP 401 `AUTH_REQUIRED`) on requests without `request.state.session`. By the time the bot's bearer reaches the api, BotAuth must already have injected the service-account session — otherwise SessionStub 401s the bot's call before BotAuth's session population can apply. BotAuth must also run before CSRF because CSRF reads `request.state.is_bot_authenticated` to decide whether to skip the cookie+header double-submit check for bot calls (the bot has no cookies; forcing CSRF would mean two secrets to manage).
- **Decision: lazy-import `SessionContext` inside `BotAuthMiddleware.dispatch`.** The natural import path (`services.api.middleware` → `services.api.session` → `services.api.config` → `services.api.middleware`) forms a cycle at module-load time because `services.api.session.SessionStubMiddleware` already imports `services.api.config.APISettings`. Lazy-importing `SessionContext` inside the dispatch method (which runs only after the module graph has fully settled) breaks the cycle without restructuring either module. Safe at request time; not safe at module-load time.
- **Decision: bot's `/halt` confirm view 60s timeout + invoker-only + consumed-once.** The 60s window is long enough for a deliberate "read the side-effects, then click" pause; short enough that a stale ephemeral message after operator distraction doesn't stay clickable. Invoker-only `interaction_check` is defense against shared-guild scenarios (single-operator system today; future-proofs against a junior-operator addition or shared-guild assistant). Consumed-once flag guards against fast double-clicks racing two api calls — discord.py disables the view on the first click but the race window exists.
- **Decision: tests target `POST /api/system/kill-switch/invoke` for the bot-auth integration coverage.** The invoke handler depends only on `get_session_context` (no DB-touching repo dep), so unit tests can exercise the full middleware chain (BotAuth + CSRF bypass + SessionStub injection-or-skip + route handler reaches its 501 stub) without spinning up Postgres or a testcontainer. The other repository-coupled endpoints (`/api/system/kill-switch` GET, `/api/positions/current`) would need `app.dependency_overrides[get_session]` wiring; that's a Phase 1 integration-test concern when the dispatcher lands the real handler.

Root cause: `@tailwindcss/forms` plugin (enabled in `apps/web/tailwind.config.ts`) resets all form inputs to a white-bg + dark-text default, overriding the dark theme's `:root { color-scheme: dark; }`. **Fix:** added `@layer base` CSS in `apps/web/src/app/globals.css` that themes all `input[type=text|password|email|number|tel|search|url]` + `textarea` + `select` with `bg-bg-elevated text-text-primary`, plus a `text-text-muted` placeholder. `@layer base` means per-input className utilities still take precedence when intentional. Deployed via `docker compose build nextjs && docker compose up -d nextjs`.
  - **Bug 3 (services/api/routes/setup.py) — fixed mid-ceremony as commit `5084d74 fix(api): verify_token must persist ceremony in CeremonyStore`:** After Bug 2's fix, operator could submit Step 1 (token verify) successfully → page advanced to Step 2 (WebAuthn register) → clicking "Register passkey" returned 401 with "Ceremony session is invalid or expired" within 5 seconds (well inside the 30-min TTL). Day-21's PR #70 (which added the CeremonyStore + the 4-step wizard endpoints) tested the wizard endpoints with stub ceremony state injected directly into the store; the integration with the Day-5 route was never tested end-to-end. Subsequent wizard endpoints (webauthn/register/challenge + register/verify + totp/enroll-challenge + totp/setup-verify + backup-codes/generate) all use `_get_ceremony(store, body.ceremony_session_id, expected_kind="setup")` which fails with 401 INVALID_CEREMONY_SESSION when the lookup misses. **Fix:** inject `CeremonyStore` via `Depends(get_ceremony_store)` and replace the UUID7 mint with `await store.create_setup_ceremony(setup_token_uuid=row.token_uuid, intended_role=row.intended_role)`. Also dropped the now-unused `uuid_utils` import. Regression test `test_verify_token_persists_ceremony_in_store` in `tests/unit/test_api_setup_token.py` explicitly fetches the returned `ceremony_session_id` from the store + asserts `kind`/`intended_role`/`setup_token_uuid` are populated, locking the handshake going forward. Existing test relaxed length check (CeremonyStore.mint_key uses token_urlsafe(16) ≈ 22 chars vs the prior UUID7's 36) + injects a fresh CeremonyStore per test to avoid singleton pollution. 720/720 unit tests pass (was 719 + 1 new regression).

- **Process lesson — token-in-chat leak discipline (3 leaks in this single session):** Three times during the ceremony, I echoed secret values to stdout that the operator dutifully pasted back. The first leak was the original `sops -d ... | grep` whose output included the full key values; the operator caught this and rotated immediately. The second was a `docker compose logs api ... | grep SETUP_TOKEN_EMITTED | head -5` pattern where the structlog `SETUP_TOKEN_EMITTED` line includes `raw_token` in its JSON payload — `head -5` printed it to stdout. The third was an api-log grep filtered by `verify-token|webauthn|register|ceremony|invalid` which matched the `SETUP_TOKEN_EMITTED` lines (because of `verify-token` in the path) and surfaced two raw tokens. **Forward rule added to dev-guide §1.5 LOCKED:** anything that might contain `raw_token` / `password` / `api_bearer` / `encryption_key` / `secret_key` / `private_key` patterns goes to a file with `chmod 600` and the verification step is `wc -l` (count only) — never `head`, `cat`, `grep` displayed to stdout. Even for diagnostic visibility. Counts/line-numbers/SHAs are paste-safe; raw values are not. The discipline rule is now: **if I write a grep pattern that COULD match a log line containing a secret, the grep output goes to a file by default — visibility is opt-in via an additional explicit step**. This matches the Day-1 QC token rotation incident precedent and the subsequent Day-3 sops setup discipline (`Docs/decisions-log.md` 2026-05-05 entries).

Single public entrypoint: `apply_state_transition(*, plan, db, account_id, env, phase_at_emit) -> AppliedStateTransition`. The two-step plan-then-apply pattern is identical to `services.risk.sizing` (Day 6-9 PR #28) and `services.reconciliation.recon` (Day 9 PR #42). **Audit-first ordering** per backend-spec §2.10.1: iterates `plan.audit_events` in order calling `append_audit_event` (each event commits in its own SERIALIZABLE transaction; the writer manages the advisory lock + retry); then opens a separate transaction for the `risk_state` UPSERT (UPDATE prior `is_current=TRUE` row to FALSE, INSERT fresh row with `is_current=TRUE` carrying the LAST audit event's UUID as the FK). Returns `AppliedStateTransition(state_transition_audit_event_uuid, new_state, new_severity)` — Literal-typed for mypy narrowing at the route layer. **Why no SSE emit here:** keeping the risk layer free of api-layer dependencies preserves the option to call the same dispatch entry-point from non-api callers (a future scheduler worker, a Discord bot path that hits the DB directly). The route handler emits SSE after this returns. **A01 BINDS** (every audit row routes through `append_audit_event`). **A02 BINDS** (`services/risk/**`). **A04 BINDS** (every event_type is in the locked taxonomy). **A06 enforced** (all timestamps tz-aware UTC). **A05 N/A** (no monetary values).

- **Spec reference:** Day 25 PR #76 merged earlier in the day; carryover smoke per the Day-12/14/17/24 operator-delegated SSH pattern. Operator authorization: "you take care of it" — Claude drove the deploy + smoke end-to-end via `ssh root@178.156.239.84`, with operator merging the two fix-up PRs (#77 + #78) inline.
- **What happened (timeline, ~50 min wall-time):**
  - **20:08 UTC — initial deploy.** SSH baseline check (`HEAD=5084d74 Day 24 mid-ceremony fix`; all 6 containers healthy; audit_log empty per the standing Day-12 baseline). `git pull --ff-only origin main` advanced `5084d74 → 99c9f2f` (PR #76). `docker compose build api` + `up -d --force-recreate api` brought the new image up healthy in 12s.
  - **20:14 UTC — first invoke smoke: DP-021 surfaced.** `docker compose exec -T -e BOT_BEARER=<extracted-via-Python-stdout-into-shell-var-never-echoed> api curl -sS -X POST .../api/system/kill-switch/invoke` returned **HTTP 500** with `sqlalchemy.exc.InvalidRequestError: A transaction is already begun on this Session`. The failure was in `services/audit/writer.py:238` (`async with session.begin()` in `__aenter__`), which means the api had reached the writer but the session was already in a transaction state — violating the writer's contract at writer.py:58 ("Callers MUST NOT pass a session that already has an open transaction"). **Root cause:** FastAPI's `Depends` cache shares the same `AsyncSession` between `Phase1QueryRepo` reads (`fetch_active_account_id` + `fetch_risk_state_current`) and `apply_state_transition`. SQLAlchemy 2.0 autobegin semantics: the repo's SELECTs implicitly start a transaction; the writer then raised because a transaction was already active. Day-25 unit tests never caught this because they monkeypatched `apply_state_transition` (real writer never ran); Day-25 integration tests used a fresh session not previously touched by a repo. **State post-failure:** `risk_state=NORMAL` preserved; audit chain still empty (the writer raised in `__aenter__` BEFORE any SQL hit). No orphan data.
  - **20:15-20:24 UTC — DP-021 fix authored + tested.** Branch `claude/day25-carryover-dp021-transaction-fix` off `99c9f2f`. Fix: `await db.commit()` between the repo reads and `apply_state_transition` in both invoke + resume routes (`services/api/routes/system.py:336` + `:459`). Regression test in `tests/integration/test_kill_switch_end_to_end.py:test_apply_after_repo_reads_via_same_session_dp021` asserts BOTH directions (without commit → raises; with commit → succeeds). Unit-test fake `_NoopDbSession` gained a no-op `commit()` (route happy path calls it). All 752 tests green locally; lint + mypy clean. **PR #77 opened + operator merged inline at 20:23 UTC.**
  - **20:24-20:26 UTC — second deploy.** Pull `99c9f2f → 1aed311`; rebuild api (10s); restart. Healthy.
  - **20:25 UTC — second invoke smoke: DP-022 surfaced.** Same curl returned **HTTP 500** again, different error: `asyncpg.exceptions.InsufficientPrivilegeError: permission denied for sequence audit_log_sequence_no_seq`. **Root cause:** `alembic/versions/0006_roles.py:84` grants INSERT/SELECT on `audit_log` TABLE to `app_service` but never grants USAGE on the BIGSERIAL backing sequence `audit_log_sequence_no_seq`. The `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ... ON TABLES` clause at 0006:88-90 only covers TABLES — sequences need a separate `ON SEQUENCES` grant. Postgres' BIGSERIAL DEFAULT calls `nextval(...)` which requires USAGE on the sequence; without it the INSERT fails with SQLSTATE 42501. **Why this stayed latent for 5+ weeks:** every prior audit-writer integration test binds to the testcontainer SUPERUSER (the default postgres user); SUPERUSER has implicit grants on every object so the gap was invisible. Day-25's PR was the **first production code path** to write to `audit_log` as `app_service` — exposed immediately. Chain still empty (no SQL executed; writer raised in `nextval` before INSERT landed).
  - **20:26-20:34 UTC — DP-022 fix authored + tested.** Branch `claude/day25-carryover-dp022-audit-log-sequence-grant` off `1aed311`. New alembic migration `20260518_audit_seq_grant` (operational, idempotent; revision id kept 24-char to fit Alembic's `VARCHAR(32)` `version_num` column — the longer `20260518_audit_log_sequence_grant` (33 chars) overflowed during initial test run). Migration grants `USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCE audit_log_sequence_no_seq TO app_service` + `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO app_service` (future-proofing). Regression test `test_audit_log_insert_as_app_service_succeeds_dp022` in `tests/integration/test_audit_immutability.py` exercises the writer AS `app_service` via `SET LOCAL ROLE`. Also updated `tests/integration/test_alembic_auth_tables.py` `TestUpDownUp` to target `_AUTH_REVISION` explicitly instead of `head`/`-1` (with DP-022 sitting on top of the auth tables, `head` is no longer `20260513_auth_tables`). **PR #78 opened + operator applied risk-review-approved + merged inline at 20:35 UTC.**
  - **20:35-20:37 UTC — third deploy.** Pull `1aed311 → 7e8d5cf`. First attempted `alembic upgrade head` failed silently — current revision didn't advance — because the api Docker image hadn't been rebuilt yet (the new migration file was on the host filesystem but not in `/app/alembic/versions/` inside the running container). Lesson learned: when an alembic migration lands, the build-then-upgrade sequence is mandatory; `git pull` alone doesn't propagate the file into the container's image. After `docker compose build api && up -d --force-recreate api`, `alembic upgrade head` ran cleanly: `Running upgrade 20260513_auth_tables -> 20260518_audit_seq_grant, Grant USAGE on audit_log_sequence_no_seq to app_service (DP-022 fix)` + post-upgrade `20260518_audit_seq_grant (head)`. SUPERUSER DATABASE_URL constructed in-shell from `POSTGRES_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD` in `deploy/.env` (never echoed; sanity-checked via `${#DB_URL}` byte count only).
  - **20:37 UTC — third invoke smoke: GREEN.** Same curl finally returned **HTTP 200**: `{"risk_state":"HALT_NEW","severity":"routine","halt_reason":"manual_judgment","audit_event_uuid":"019e18c2-19a7-7482-8201-6aa4ac7ef17f","sse_sequence_no":1}`. Post-state GET `/api/system/kill-switch` confirmed: `risk_state=HALT_NEW`, `severity=routine`, `halt_reason=manual_judgment`, `last_transition_utc=2026-05-11T20:37:14.291649Z`, `last_transition_audit_event_uuid=019e18c2-19a7-7482-8201-6aa4ac7ef17f` (FK linkage from `risk_state.audit_event_uuid` → `audit_log.event_uuid` verified). **First-ever production audit_log write.**
  - **20:37 UTC — verify_chain confirms integrity.** `python -m services.audit.verify_chain --env paper` (via app_service URL) returned `CHAIN OK: 1 rows verified` + structlog `verify_chain_passed env=paper rows_walked=1`. Direct row spot-check via `app_service` SELECT confirmed: `sequence_no=1`, `event_type=state_transition_normal_to_halt`, `env=paper`, `prev_hash[0:16]=0000000000000000...` (GENESIS_HASH for first chain row), `record_hash[0:16]=ea9efc0cbdf61571...` (real SHA-256 of canonical payload + prev_hash).

- **Three latent bugs discovered + closed (Day 25 + 2 carryover fixes):**
  - **DP-021** (Day 25 PR — fixed by PR #77): FastAPI `Depends` cache shares session between repo and writer → writer raises on `session.begin()` because repo opened implicit tx. Fix: `await db.commit()` between reads and apply. Regression: `test_apply_after_repo_reads_via_same_session_dp021`.
  - **DP-022** (latent since Day 3 / alembic 0006 — fixed by PR #78): `app_service` had INSERT on `audit_log` table but no USAGE on the BIGSERIAL sequence.   - **DP-021/022 root-cause pattern (process lesson):** both bugs were invisible to CI because every prior audit-writer test ran against the testcontainer's SUPERUSER role. SUPERUSER has implicit grants on every object + no session-scope contention from FastAPI dependency caching. The first production code path that wrote to `audit_log` as the real `app_service` role inside a FastAPI route exposed BOTH gaps within ~10 minutes. **Forward rule (to add to dev-guide §6 testing patterns):** when a new prod surface writes to `audit_log`, the integration test suite MUST include at least one test that runs the writer AS `app_service` (not SUPERUSER) AND simulates the FastAPI session-sharing pattern (i.e., issue a SELECT through the session before calling the writer). - **Decisions made under §1.3 ambiguity protocol (pattern-internal):**
  - **CSV export = client-side blob, not server-side endpoint.** Frontend-spec §15.1 mandates `/api/trades/export.csv` with audit-chain anchor footer. Phase 0 trades table is empty + no anchor to anchor against. Building the server endpoint with Phase-0 empty body + footer pointing at the Day-25 first prod audit row (sequence_no=1) would be premature — the audit-anchor lookup itself needs design (server reads chain head + signs the footer via JCS hash). Defer to Phase 1+ once trades populate. The client-side blob with a 14-column subset preserves the locked-schema column ordering so future cutover is mechanical.
  - **`/api/trades/:id` returns 404 + canonical `TRADE_NOT_FOUND` envelope (NOT raw 404).** Per IG line 417 "ensures Discord deep-links don't 404" — but Next's hard 404 IS a 404 page. The right reading: the frontend should render a graceful "Trade not found" body INSTEAD of Next's hard 404 page. Backend returns canonical envelope so the frontend can detect via `error.errorCode === 'TRADE_NOT_FOUND'` and render the friendly body.
  - **No-active-account also returns 404 `TRADE_NOT_FOUND` on detail path.** Spec doesn't say — but if no account exists, no trade can possibly exist with the requested ID. Matches behavior of the list endpoint (returns empty list when no account). Alternative (`409 NO_ACTIVE_ACCOUNT`) felt wrong because the operator's question is "show me trade X" and the canonical answer is "no such trade."
  - **`id_prefix` filter Phase-1 lock.** Spec §4.1.2 lists it; Phase 2 command palette is the consumer. Lock the wire now so the palette doesn't trip a contract change later. Treat as ordinary string + escape LIKE metachars defensively.

- **Decisions made under §1.3 ambiguity protocol (pattern-internal):**
  - **Risk envelope wire shape — flat `items` list instead of nested struct.** The spec §2.6.3 displays the values as a flat list; the wire shape mirrors that for cheap iteration on the frontend. Future Phase-2 `[Propose change]` buttons attach per-item without a schema change.
  - **`source: "spec_defaults" | "parameters_table"` field on RiskEnvelopeResponse.** Operator runbook diagnostic — distinguishes "Phase 0 hasn't seeded parameters yet" from "the active set was deliberately changed". Frontend renders identically; the field only matters for debugging.
  - **Partial parameter_sets row falls back to spec defaults (not a 500).** A row that's missing canonical keys (e.g. Phase 1+ parameter-set evolution adds keys that an old row doesn't have) renders as defaults + emits a `risk_envelope_parameter_set_missing_keys` warning log. Avoids a degenerate "show some defaults + some real values" envelope.
  - **Audit cursor encoding — decimal sequence_no, NOT base64.** Different from the trades cursor (which is base64 of JSON tuple) because audit_log has a globally-unique monotonic BIGSERIAL; the decimal form is operator-readable + lock-free + no encode/decode round-trip overhead. The `INVALID_CURSOR` AppError mirrors the `_pagination.py` contract for consistency.
  - **Audit payload_preview decoded with `errors='replace'`.** A malformed JCS payload (shouldn't happen — JCS is ASCII per RFC 8785) renders as replacement characters rather than crashing the page. Replacement chars in the preview signal the operator to fetch the full row.
  - **Re-auth threshold is 4.5 min, not 5 min.** Frontend checks against a 4.5-min freshness window (30s buffer before the server's 5-min cutoff). Prevents the race condition where the page reads a barely-fresh timestamp, the user clicks RESUME, network latency carries the request past the 5-min cutoff, server returns 401. With the 30s buffer the modal opens BEFORE the server-side gate would reject — operator never sees a confusing mid-flow 401.
  - **InvokeKillSwitchModal hard-codes `trigger="manual_judgment"`.** The schema accepts 16 trigger enum values but the web UI only has one button. The other 15 are reserved for automated callers (risk_engine / agent / watchdog) wired Phase 1+. If the operator needs to log a specific trigger (e.g. recon-mismatch they observed manually), the reason text field carries that intent.
  - **`/system/audit` row click → detail page deferred.** The spec §2.6.4 calls for clicking a row → `/system/audit/:event_uuid` detail page. Phase 0 has 1 audit row + the detail page needs a richer payload format (pretty-printed JSON, hash-chain breadcrumb). Defer to Phase 1+ when audit volume + the detail-page surface land. Today the table is read-only display.
  - **TanStack table virtualization deferred for audit-log table.** Spec §2.6.4 says virtualization for large lists; Phase 0 has 1 row + the spec doesn't require it until volume > 50 rows. Defer to Phase 1+ — same lesson as Day 26 Trades CSV.

- **Pattern carved out by PR-A for future Phase-1 ingestion handlers:**
  - **session_factory > session.** When a handler does audit-write → SELECT → audit-write or audit-write → SELECT → INSERT, it MUST take a `session_factory` (not a session) and create a fresh session per DB op. The audit writer's `async with session.begin()` contract requires no-open-transaction; SELECT on a shared session triggers asyncio's autobegin which conflicts with the writer's next call. This is the second DP-021 case after Day 25's risk dispatch.
  - **Auto-bootstrap of FK-dependency rows.** When a NOT-NULL FK columns lands and the dependency table is empty by design (slippage_calibration_versions during Phase 0 bootstrap), the handler auto-bootstraps the dependency row via audit-first ordering: append `<dep>_RECALIBRATED` audit event first, then INSERT the dep row carrying that audit_event_uuid. Idempotent under race via re-read on IntegrityError. Pattern reusable for future zero-prior dependencies.
  - **Key-prefix filtering for sequence_no cursor advancement.** QC ObjectStore keys are flat strings (no nested-namespace API); the orchestrator extracts the sequence_no via regex (`(?:[^/]+/)*(\d+)\.jsonl$`) and filters > `cursor.last_consumed_sequence_no`. Keys that don't match the pattern are skipped + logged but don't fail the cycle. Reusable for PR-C/D when ack files + state snapshots have similar shapes.

### 2026-05-12 — Day 28 carryover — PR-A deploy + 2 hot-fix follow-ups (PR #85 + #86) + QC tier blocker discovery + Phase-1 architectural pivot to LEAN Local + IBKR paper (Option 4)

- **Spec reference:** PR #84 merged at 23:55 UTC. Carryover deploy follows the Day 24-27 operator-delegated SSH pattern; operator authorization: "You can deploy now." Three sequential discoveries during the deploy: (1) DP-023 string-to-Literal[int] coercion bug; (2) DP-024 sops field `organization_id` was being passed as Basic-auth username when QC's API actually expects a numeric `user_id` for that field AND a separate `organizationId` POST parameter; (3) DP-025 QC subscription tier blocks `/object/get` entirely with the message "Due to data licensing restrictions, export from the object-store can only be enabled for Institutional accounts." DP-025 is a **scope-level blocker** — the entire backend-spec §1.4/§2.11/§4.5.1 ObjectStore polling architecture is infeasible on the operator's current QC subscription tier.

- **VPS baseline (pre-deploy 23:55 UTC):** HEAD `c2f0468` (Day 27 carryover close). All 6 containers healthy. `audit_log` 2 rows. `risk_state` CONVALESCENT.

- **Deploy attempt #1 (00:30 UTC) — DP-023 caught:**
  - `git pull --ff-only origin main` advanced VPS to `7359f9d` (PR #84 squash-merge — PR-A's 18 files / 4014 insertions).
  - `docker compose build qc_adapter` succeeded in 14.4s.
  - `docker compose up -d qc_adapter` succeeded; container started; first boot crashed in a restart loop with: `ValidationError: phase_at_emit Input should be 0, 1, 2 or 3 [type=literal_error, input_value='0', input_type=str]`.
  - **DP-023:** `docker-compose.yml` passes `QC_ADAPTER_PHASE_AT_EMIT="0"` as an env var (all docker env vars are strings). `pydantic-settings` does NOT auto-coerce strings to `Literal[0, 1, 2, 3]` integer literals — strict-match by default.
  - **Fix:** `@field_validator("phase_at_emit", mode="before")` coerces incoming strings to int before Literal validation runs. Shipped as PR #85 (regular review; `services/qc_adapter/**` on hot-fix whitelist).
  - **PR #85 timeline:** opened 00:40 → 12 CI checks green @ 00:55 → squash-merged @ 01:05 as commit `9832eae`.
  - **Pattern carved out:** any pydantic-settings config field declared with integer Literal values needs a `mode="before"` validator if it's expected to come in via docker-compose env vars. The api/discord_bot configs use string Literals so don't hit this; qc_adapter was the first case.

- **Deploy attempt #2 (01:10 UTC) — auth fails with QC "UserID not valid":**
  - VPS pulled `9832eae` (PR #85). Rebuild + recreate qc_adapter. Container boot clean: `qc_adapter_booting → qc_adapter_account_resolved → qc_adapter_orchestrator_started`. All 3 directory loops alive at 60/60/5s cadences.
  - **But:** every list_keys call returns `QC success=false for '/object-store/list': ['UserID not valid (a3d7fe4da507e67661877333cd7273c5) REF #m2scDQ8GD7']`. The 32-char hex value `a3d7fe4da507e67661877333cd7273c5` is the operator's QC organization slug, NOT the numeric User ID that QC's HTTP Basic auth requires.
  - **DP-024:** The Q1 ambiguity I surfaced at session start ("Is `quantconnect.organization_id` actually the user_id used for Basic auth?") was wrong in my default — `organization_id` in the sops template was misleadingly named; QC actually distinguishes between `userId` (numeric, Basic auth username) and `organizationId` (hex slug, POST body parameter for ObjectStore endpoints).
  - Operator pulled their numeric QC User ID from `quantconnect.com → avatar → My Account` (6-digit numeric value) and updated sops: dropped `quantconnect.organization_id` + added `quantconnect.user_id: <numeric>`. Committed locally on VPS in 2 commits (`4b4cadb` + `8cc8658`).
  - **Code-side rename:** PR #86 shipped the matching change — `services/qc_adapter/entrypoint.py` reads `quantconnect.user_id` (was `organization_id`); `deploy/sops/secret_schemas/{paper,live}.template.yaml` renamed + inline-commented the field; `deploy/qc_adapter/README.md` + 3 module docstrings updated. **VPS deploy key is read-only**; the 2 operator commits had to be cherry-picked locally via `git format-patch` + `git am` before pushing from my workstation (carved-out pattern: any VPS-originated commits route through this format-patch → am → push cycle until the deploy key gets write access).
  - **PR #86 timeline:** opened 01:35 → 12 CI checks green @ 01:39 → squash-merged @ 01:40 as commit `a27884a`.

- **Deploy attempt #3 (01:40 UTC) — DP-025 discovered (the hard stop):**
  - VPS pulled `a27884a` (PR #86). Hard-reset VPS branch to origin/main (VPS had 2 local sops commits that were squash-superseded by `a27884a`; `git reset --hard origin/main` was the safe path since the contents already merged via the PR).
  - Rebuild --no-cache + recreate qc_adapter. Container boot still fail-closed at entrypoint with `quantconnect.user_id missing or placeholder in /run/secrets/decrypted.yaml`. Root cause: the `/opt/trading/secrets-decrypted/decrypted.yaml` host file is the pre-decrypted artifact mounted into the container; it was stale (Day 24 ceremony version, still had `organization_id`). Manually re-decrypted via `sops --decrypt secrets/paper.enc.yaml > /opt/trading/secrets-decrypted/decrypted.yaml && chmod 600 ...` to pull in the operator's `user_id` field. Restarted container.
  - **DP-026 (process-level):** the sops re-decryption is not automated; the VPS bringup script (`deploy/day5-bringup.sh`) handles initial decryption but every subsequent sops change requires a manual re-decrypt step. The runbooks document this implicitly (sops edit → commit → push → re-decrypt → recreate); should be made explicit in `deploy/qc_adapter/README.md` Step 1.5 OR automated via a watcher.
  - Post-restart, the auth pair worked — no more `UserID not valid` errors. But every list call returned `QC response not JSON for '/object-store/list': Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`. Empty body / non-JSON response.
  - **Direct curl probe from the `trading_egress` Docker network** (using `docker run --rm --network trading_egress curlimages/curl`):
    - `POST /api/v2/authenticate` with the new Basic-auth pair → `{"success":true}` ✅ (auth pair validated)
    - `POST /api/v2/object-store/list` → returns the QC homepage 404 HTML (endpoint path is wrong)
    - `POST /api/v2/object/list` (singular!) with `path=events/` → `{"errors":["Required parameter organizationId is missing."],"success":false}` — endpoint exists; needs `organizationId` POST parameter
    - `POST /api/v2/object/list` with `organizationId=<32-char-hex>&path=heartbeat/` → `{"objects":[...124 files...], "success":true}` — works; the operator's QC algorithm has been writing one heartbeat JSON per day since 2026-01-01
    - `POST /api/v2/object/get` for any key → **`{"errors":["Due to data licensing restrictions, export from the object-store can only be enabled for Institutional accounts. If you're interested in enabling this feature for your organization please contact support@quantconnect.com to learn more."],"success":false}`** ❌
  - **DP-025 (the scope-level blocker):** QC's public REST API `/object/get` endpoint is gated behind the **Institutional subscription tier**. The operator's current tier allows `/object/list` (metadata only) but blocks content fetch. The entire backend-spec §1.4 + §2.11 + §4.5.1 ObjectStore polling architecture is **infeasible** on this tier — the orchestrator can enumerate keys but cannot download their contents, so signal/order/fill/recon events cannot be ingested.
  - The QC adapter container was stopped cleanly at 01:43 UTC (was in retry-and-backoff loop; not productive without `/object/get` access; running it indefinitely would burn auth-call quota for no gain). `audit_log` row count unchanged at 2; `signals` row count = 0 (graceful failure semantics worked as designed — no rogue writes during the retry storms).

- **Operator decision @ 02:00 UTC: Option 4 — LEAN Local + IBKR paper (pull Phase 2 architecture forward to Phase 1):**

  Four architectural options were surfaced:

  | Option | Description | Reliability | Cost | Verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | Upgrade QC subscription to Institutional | 9/10 | $200+/mo | Rejected — exceeds Phase-0 budget |
  | 2 | QC algorithm `WebRequest`s directly to backend `/api/internal/qc/events` | 6/10 (latency in algo hot loop + no QC-side persistence + in-algo retry queue is non-trivial + auth secret in QC algorithm config) | $0 incremental | Fallback if IBKR pivot blocked |
  | 3 | Defer Phase-1 live trading | n/a | $0 | Rejected — postpones ceremony indefinitely |
  | **4** | **LEAN Local on VPS + IBKR paper account (backend-spec §1.5 Phase 2 architecture, pulled forward)** | **8/10** | **$0 incremental (IBKR paper is free; LEAN is OSS; ~$0-25/mo for real-time IBKR market data if needed)** | **CHOSEN** |

  **Why Option 4 wins:**
  - Spec was always going to cut over to LEAN Local + direct IBKR at Phase 2 (backend-spec §1.5); doing it now skips ObjectStore polling entirely instead of building a 5-PR bridge and immediately retiring it.
  - LEAN is open-source; `quantconnect/lean` Docker image is documented + maintained.
  - IBKR paper trading is free + behaviorally close to live; the simulated fill engine is the strongest test environment available pre-live.
  - Eliminates QC subscription tier dependency; eliminates the QC-side persistence-vs-network-reliability tradeoff Option 2 had to solve.
  - The 30-session minimum from backend-spec §11.1 still holds (the spirit is "test the SYSTEM, not the broker") — restart the session counter at the IBKR cutover.

  **Catches the operator flagged:**
  - **IBKR Pro account is approved BUT futures-trading approval is still pending.** IBKR paper accounts get a simulated full-feature environment regardless of live futures approval — paper trades on `/MES`, `/MNQ`, `/MCL` should work pre-futures-approval (IBKR paper grants broad simulated permissions). Worth verifying in the new session before committing wired code.
  - All 5 PRs of the original Phase-1-onset chain (PR-A merged + PR-B/C/D/E planned) need to be re-spec'd. The work doesn't shrink — it shifts from "QC poll layer + instruction protocol + ack layer" to "LEAN Local container + IBKR Gateway container + ib-async wiring + direct fill ingestion via FlexQuery + IBKR statement reconciliation." Similar cumulative time (~10-14h); different scaffolding.

  **What stays:**
  - **PR-A's merged code stays in place but goes dormant.** `services/qc_adapter/**` remains importable + tested but no longer runs in production. The container is stopped + the service block in `docker-compose.yml` will be profile-gated under `qc_adapter_backfill` (Phase 2+ retained role per backend-spec §1.4 line 233 "retained for backfill audit reads only"). PR-A's 50 tests still pass + still gate CI.
  - **Audit log integrity is preserved.** `verify_chain --env paper` returns `CHAIN OK: 2 rows verified` (genesis → seq=1 Day 25 halt → seq=2 Day 27 resume). The pivot doesn't disturb the chain; new writes from LEAN Local / ib-async route through the same `append_audit_event` writer.
  - **Strategy code stays.** `strategies/v1_trend_following/{parameters,indicators,signals,strategy,sizing_trace,audit_events}.py` is broker-agnostic and runs identically under LEAN Local. The QC algorithm wrapper at `lean/v1_qc_algorithm.py` becomes the LEAN-Local entrypoint (no longer "QC's algorithm runtime"); the file may be renamed during the pivot.
  - **All 7 currently-running services stay (api, caddy, discord_bot, nextjs, postgres, qc_adapter [stopped], webhook_pusher).** Phase-1 pivot adds 2 new services (`lean_local` + `ib_gateway`) profile-gated until the pivot PRs land.

- **Pattern carved out by Day 28 carryover for future architectural blockers:**
  - **Smoke against real external APIs early.** PR-A had A27 satisfied via the operator runbook (`deploy/qc_adapter/README.md`), which itself satisfied dev-guide §6.8 alternative (b). BUT the runbook is a checklist; it does NOT exercise the platform contract before deploy. If we'd run a `curl /authenticate` + `curl /object/get` test during PR-A scope-triage (e.g. by adding the curl probes to the operator runbook as Step 0.5 "verify the credentials work AND `get` is permitted before building any code"), DP-025 would have been caught BEFORE writing 4000+ lines of polling-architecture code. **New rule for §6.8 / A27 satisfiers on third-party API integrations:** the operator runbook MUST include an end-to-end smoke that exercises the **most-restricted endpoint** the integration depends on, not just the auth endpoint. For QC ObjectStore: that's `/object/get`, not `/authenticate`. Pattern reusable for IBKR (smoke `placeOrder` + `cancelOrder` paper-account round-trip before wiring `services/execution/`), Resend (smoke `POST /emails` before wiring webhook_pusher's email path), etc.
  - **VPS deploy key write access.** Day 28 hit it twice — PR-A hot-fix had to be rebased onto stale main; PR-B (this doc carryover) is again pushed from my workstation because VPS `git push` errors with "The key you are authenticating with has been marked as read only." Either (a) give the VPS deploy key write access (security risk: any code path that lands a malicious commit on disk could git-push to main) OR (b) keep the current pattern of `format-patch → am → push from workstation` (cleaner security boundary; just an extra friction step that operator workflows should bake in).
  - **DP-pattern numbering scales linearly.** DP-001 through DP-026 in ~28 days; ~1 new DP per session. Future sessions will continue to discover platform-contract assumptions that don't survive contact. Document discipline per dev-guide §1.3 (escalate over decide) is the right default; some DPs only surface at deploy time, not code review.

Day 28 carryover closed at 02:00 UTC after PR-A's 18-files-4014-insertions code shipped clean through 3 sequential CI runs (PR #84 → #85 → #86) and 3 sequential VPS deploy attempts — each successive deploy resolved one platform-contract assumption that the previous deploy uncovered. PR-A merged. PR #85 (DP-023 string-to-int coercion fix) merged. PR #86 (DP-024 organization_id → user_id rename) merged. The qc_adapter container booted cleanly with correct auth on the third attempt — but **DP-025 (QC Institutional-tier gating of `/object/get`) is a scope-level blocker** for the entire backend-spec §1.4 / §2.11 / §4.5.1 ObjectStore polling architecture on the operator's current QC subscription tier. Operator decision @ 02:00 UTC: **Option 4 — pivot to LEAN Local + IBKR paper, pulling backend-spec §1.5 Phase 2 architecture forward into Phase 1.** Audit chain integrity preserved (2 rows; `verify_chain --env paper` clean). qc_adapter container stopped + its merged code surface stays in place under the `qc_adapter_backfill` profile gate (Phase 2+ retained role per spec §1.4 line 233). 4 new DPs (DP-023 through DP-026) added to the register. Pattern carved out: §6.8 / A27 operator runbooks for third-party API integrations MUST smoke the **most-restricted endpoint** the integration depends on, not just the auth endpoint — DP-025 was caught at deploy time when a curl probe during PR-A scope-triage would have surfaced it pre-code. ### 2026-05-12 — Day 29 — Phase-1 architecture pivot — QC ObjectStore → LEAN Local + direct IBKR (DP-025 → Option 4)

> **This entry is the canonical record of the 2026-05-12 architecture pivot.** Future agents reading the specs should consult this entry to understand why the foundation docs read the way they do post-pivot. It documents (a) what changed in each foundation doc, (b) what the new code surfaces will look like across Pivot-PR-A through Pivot-PR-E, (c) which references in the docs were NOT touched and where pre-pivot text remains for institutional memory, and (d) the process patterns carved out for future pivots.

- **Spec reference:** `Docs/decisions-log.md` 2026-05-12 Day 28 carryover entry (the prior entry above this one) — full DP-025 discovery narrative + Option 4 selection rationale. The 6 affected foundation docs and their pre-pivot section anchors are listed in the brief that initiated this session (preserved in conversation transcript; the key sections are `Docs/backend-spec.md` §1.2/1.3/1.4/1.5/2.1.1/2.3/2.5/2.6/2.11/3.19/4.5.1/4.5.2/6.6.1 + `Docs/claude-dev-guide.md` §1.5 + [A13] + `implementation-guide.md` §3 Week 7 Thu + §4 Phase 1 milestone + §5 Phase 2 milestone + §8 DPR + `Docs/frontend-spec.md` §2 system page row + `Docs/ai-and-strategy-overview.md` Phase 1/Phase 2 narrative + §9 phase changes table + `CLAUDE.md` orientation surface).

- **Stage 0 PR scope (this entry's PR):** **doc-only**; touches no production code; regular review (no `risk-review-approved` label required because no whitelist paths are modified). 6 foundation docs + this decisions-log entry are the totality of the diff. The 5 Stage-1 PRs (Pivot-PR-A through Pivot-PR-E) deliver the new code surfaces and ship over the following 1-2 days.

- **Why pivot now vs. defer:**
  - The pre-pivot Phase 1 plan was built on a critical assumption (the operator's QC subscription tier supports `/object/get`) that turned out to be false at deploy time. The 5-PR Phase-1-onset build chain (PR-A QC adapter fetcher merged Day 28; PR-B/C/D/E planned) was authored against that assumption.
  - Continuing on the pre-pivot path would have required either (a) upgrading to QC Institutional (~$500-1000/mo; outside the $200/mo soft budget ceiling), (b) building an Option-2 bridge (QC algorithm `WebRequest` direct posts; new in-algo retry queue + auth secret managed inside the QC algo's code), or (c) deferring Phase-1 live trading.
  - Option 4 (pivot to LEAN Local + direct IBKR) is strictly better than (b) on architecture quality: lower latency (≤5s vs 20s round-trip), no third-party intermediary, no QC-tier-specific risks. It IS the originally-planned Phase 2 architecture (spec §1.3) — operationally proven design, just pulled forward by ~3 months.
  - Day 1-28 hardening built all the supporting infrastructure: audit chain writer, risk engine, signal sizing, web UI, Discord bot, ib_gateway docker pattern is well-documented, ib-async is a mature OSS library. The remaining gap is: 5 PRs to deliver the new pipeline + 6 foundation docs to reflect the new architecture.
